title: Grade 4 Science — Tue, Jun 10
description: Food & Nutrition — Day 2 of 5: Carbohydrates and fats
subject: science

questions.question: Carbohydrates are also called ____ foods.
questions.explanation: Carbohydrates give us quick energy for daily activities. They are called 'energy foods'.

questions.question: Which test is used to check if a food contains starch?
questions.explanation: Iodine solution turns blue-black in the presence of starch. This is the iodine test for starch.

questions.question: Which of the following foods is rich in carbohydrates?
questions.explanation: Roti (wheat bread) is rich in carbohydrates (starch). Rice, bread, potatoes, and sugar are also carbohydrate-rich.

questions.question: Sugarcane is sweet because it contains a type of carbohydrate called:
questions.explanation: Sucrose is the sugar found in sugarcane. It is a carbohydrate that gives a sweet taste and quick energy.

questions.question: Fats are important because they:
questions.explanation: Fats store energy for later use and provide a protective cushion around body organs like kidneys.

questions.question: Which of these is a plant source of fat?
questions.explanation: Groundnut (peanut) oil is a plant-based fat. Other plant fats include coconut oil, mustard oil, and sunflower oil.

questions.question: Which of these is an animal source of fat?
questions.explanation: Butter is made from milk fat — it is an animal source of fat, along with ghee, cream, and fish oil.

questions.question: The paper test for fat: if you rub food on paper and it leaves a ____ spot, it contains fat.
questions.explanation: Fatty foods leave a greasy, transparent (oily) mark on paper. This is a simple test to detect fat in food.

questions.question: Eating too many carbohydrates (like sweets and junk food) can lead to:
questions.explanation: Excess sugar and refined carbohydrates can cause weight gain and tooth decay if eaten too often.

questions.question: Which of the following contains both carbohydrates and fat?
questions.explanation: Peanut butter contains starch and sugar (carbohydrates) from peanuts and also has significant fat content.

questions.question: Dietary fibre is a type of carbohydrate that:
options: Cannot be digested but helps bowel movement
questions.explanation: Fibre (roughage) is indigestible carbohydrate that helps food move through the intestines and prevents constipation.

questions.question: Which of these foods is a good source of dietary fibre?
questions.explanation: Whole grains, fruits, and vegetables are rich in dietary fibre, which aids digestion.

questions.question: Potatoes contain large amounts of:
questions.explanation: Potatoes are mainly starch (a complex carbohydrate) and are a major energy food in Indian meals.

questions.question: Fats help the body absorb vitamins:
questions.explanation: Vitamins A, D, E, and K are fat-soluble — they need dietary fat to be absorbed by the body.

questions.question: Which of these is the body's preferred quick fuel?
questions.explanation: Carbohydrates are broken down into glucose — the body's fastest and preferred energy source for activities.
